title: Turning the chatbot on and choosing where it runs
summary: The chatbot's master switch, which channels it answers on, your office hours and the away message.

body.text: The **Chatbot** page controls the assistant that answers customers automatically on WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram and Telegram — greeting them, offering menus, answering questions and handing over to your team.
The master switch
The **Chatbot** switch at the top turns everything on or off. When it's off, **no** automatic replies go out on any channel, whatever else is set.
Where it runs & how

items: **Guided flow (menus)** — runs your published flow: tappable menus that lead to answers, bookings and the AI, on every connected channel. Turn it off and the bot only uses simple keyword replies.
**Messenger & Instagram DMs** — also runs the published flow on Facebook Messenger and Instagram messages.

body.text: Press **Open flow builder** to design the conversation itself — see **Building chatbot flows: the flow library**.
Office hours & away message

items: Open **Office hours & away message**.
Set your opening times and **Days**.
Write the **After-hours away message**.
Press **Save bot settings**.

body.text: The away message is used after hours when the AI assistant is off. Public holidays and days you're closed come from **Settings → Public holidays**, and a flow's **Opening hours** step treats them as closed.
A customer gets the away message at most once every 4 hours, so nobody is sent the same reply over and over.
Connecting a channel doesn't switch the chatbot on there — it only brings messages into the inbox. The chatbot answers only where you've switched it on here.

title: The AI assistant, approved knowledge and FAQ answers
summary: Let the chatbot answer open questions from your prices and approved facts, give exact answers to common questions, and see what it couldn't answer.

body.text: Besides menus, the chatbot can answer questions in its own words, and give exact, approved answers to common questions. All of this is on the **Chatbot** page.
AI replies to open questions

Turn on **AI replies to open questions** to let the assistant answer things like "Do you deliver to Durban?" conversationally. It uses only what you've given it: your live product prices and colours, your opening hours, the brief below, and your approved knowledge. It won't make up prices, specifications, stock or dates.

items: Turn on **AI replies to open questions**.
Fill in **About us / policies (short global brief)** — your tone, where you are, and facts that rarely change.
Put detailed policies and specifications into the knowledge workspace instead (below), so each can be checked and given an end date.
Press **Save bot settings**.

body.text: The assistant hands the customer to a person when they want to order or pay, book a particular date or test drive, have a complaint, ask something it doesn't know, or ask for a person.
Approved knowledge
Press **Open knowledge workspace** to manage the facts the chatbot may use — policies, specifications, excerpts from your documents.

items: Under **Add knowledge draft**, write the precise fact, optionally pick the **Library source** it comes from, and press **Add draft**.
New and edited entries stay as private drafts. An owner approves each one separately before the chatbot can use it.
Give an entry **Valid from** and **Valid until** dates for things that expire, such as a promotion.
Use **Test an AI answer** to see how the chatbot would answer a question with what's approved.

body.text: Editing an approved entry returns it to **Draft**, so a changed fact needs approving again before customers see it.
**Questions the chatbot couldn't answer** lists what customers asked that it had no answer for. Press **Draft an answer** and a draft is prepared for you to check and approve.
FAQ pathways: exact answers
For common questions where the wording must be exactly right, add a pathway. When a customer's question matches, the bot sends your approved answer word for word.

items: Under **FAQ pathways**, press **+ Add pathway**.
Describe when it applies, for example "asking about delivery or how they get the vehicle".
Write the exact answer to send.
Tick **Hand off after this answer** if a person should follow up.
Press **Add pathway**.

body.text: Voice notes
Customers' WhatsApp voice notes are turned into text so the bot can answer them. A **Voice-note transcription key (OpenAI Whisper)** is an optional fallback; leave it blank to keep the saved one.

title: Telegram
summary: How Telegram chats reach the chatbot and inbox, and who connects it.

body.text: Telegram runs the same published chatbot flow as your other channels, and its chats appear in the Social inbox.
Telegram is connected once for the whole CRM by your CRM provider, so you won't find it under your own Integrations. Ask them if you'd like it switched on.
For the CRM provider: connecting a Telegram bot

items: In Telegram, message **@BotFather** and create a new bot. It gives you a token that looks like 123456789:ABCdef…
Open **Settings → Integrations → Telegram**, paste it into **Bot token** and press **Connect**.
The card shows **Connected** once Telegram accepts it. Nothing needs setting up on Telegram's side.

body.text: If the card says **Token saved, but Telegram didn't accept the webhook — nothing arrives**, no messages are reaching the CRM. Disconnect and connect again with the token from @BotFather.

title: Building chatbot flows: the flow library
summary: Create a flow from a template or blank, edit it as a draft, test it, and publish it when it's ready for customers.

body.text: A **flow** is a conversation the chatbot has with customers — the greeting, the menus, the questions it asks and where each answer leads. You design flows in the **Flow builder**. Customers only ever see a flow once you **publish** it; until then you can change it freely.
Starting a flow

items: Open the **Flow builder** (from the Chatbot page, **Open flow builder**).
Choose a starter under **Start from a template**, or **Blank flow** to start from nothing. Press **Use template**.
The new flow opens as a draft — change anything you like.

body.text: Working on a draft

items: Press **Edit draft** to open the canvas.
Add steps and connect them — see **Flow builder steps explained** and **Chatbot flow builder: working on a flow**.
Try it in the test chat to see exactly what a customer would see.
Save as you go. Saving doesn't change what customers see.

body.text: Publishing

Each flow shows whether it's ready: **Graph compiles** (every step is complete and connected), **Channel compatible** (it works on each connected channel — for example WhatsApp shows at most three buttons) and **Saved draft differs** (you've changed it since the last publish).

items: Press **Review & publish**.
If it says **Fix publish errors first**, open the draft and fix what's listed.
Publish. The flow shows **Live** and customers get the new version.

body.text: Publishing saves a fixed version for customers. Changes you make afterwards stay in the draft until you publish again.
Taking a flow offline
Press **Take offline** on a live flow to stop customers reaching it. The draft is kept, so you can publish it again later.

title: Flow builder steps explained
summary: What each kind of step in a chatbot flow does, and when to use it.

body.text: A flow is made of steps joined together. Add a step from the step list on the canvas (or hold Ctrl/⌘ and click an empty spot), then fill it in on the right.
Talking to the customer

rows: Offers buttons or a list, each leading somewhere different
Asks a question and keeps the answer, for example their name or email
Asks the customer to send a photo or document, saved with their record
Sends a picture with an optional caption
Sends one of your files, such as a brochure or price list
Sends your business's (or a staff member's) contact card
Sends your live price list, your colours, or text you write
Lets the AI reply conversationally, using only what you've given it

body.text: Getting things done

rows: Offers real open booking times and reserves the chosen one in the diary
Creates a service request, test drive or lead, or finds or updates work in the CRM
Tags the customer, sets their salesperson or moves their deal
Enrols the customer in one of your Journeys
Alerts a team member while the bot carries on — the customer isn't handed over
Passes the conversation to your team
Fetches information from another web service (for technical set-ups)

body.text: Deciding where to go

rows: Goes one way or another based on a rule
Goes one of several ways depending on a value
Goes one way when you're open and another when closed, including public holidays
Stores or changes a value to use later
Picks details such as a name or date out of what the customer wrote
Pauses quietly; the flow carries on with the customer's next message once the time has passed
Runs another published flow, so common parts can be reused
Jumps to another step — for example back to the menu — without drawing a line

body.text: For your team only

items: **Note** — a sticky note on the canvas. Never sent.
**Group** — a coloured box to frame a section. Never sent.

body.text: Using what the customer told you
Anything saved by **Ask & save** can be used later with double braces, for example `{{name}}`. The name, phone number and email you collect are used automatically by booking and CRM steps.
For a real, dated booking use **Workshop slots** — the chosen time is saved as `{{slot}}`. A **CRM / booking action** on its own logs a request for your team to confirm.
On WhatsApp, a menu with more than three options is shown as a list instead of buttons. The builder warns you.

title: Competitor intelligence: watching your competitors
summary: List the competitors that matter, and watch their pricing, product and social pages for important changes.

body.text: **Competitor intelligence** keeps an eye on the competitors that matter to you and tells you when something important changes on their public pages — a new price, a new product, a promotion.
Adding a competitor

items: Press **Add competitor**.
Enter the **Name**, and optionally their **Website** and **Notes** on why they matter.
Choose a **Tier**: **Tier 1 · critical**, **Tier 2 · important** or **Tier 3 · watch**.
Save. Their profile opens.

body.text: The list shows each competitor's tier, how many pages are watched and how many changes are waiting for you, with critical ones in red.
Choosing pages to watch

items: On the competitor's profile, under **Watched pages**, enter a label and the page's web address.
Pick what kind of page it is — pricing, product, news, blog, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube or other.
Press **Add page to watch**.
Use **Check now** to look at a page straight away, or **Remove** to stop watching it.

body.text: Only public web pages can be watched. Removing a page also removes its saved history.
Changing competitors and their pages needs the permission to manage competitors. Deleting a competitor moves it, with its history, to Trash.

title: AI research and reviewing competitor changes
summary: Let the AI find a competitor's pages and write a briefing, and work through the changes it spots.

body.text: Letting the AI do the legwork

items: **Discover sources** — the AI finds the competitor's main pages and social profiles and adds them to **Watched pages**.
**Run research** — the AI researches the competitor online and writes a briefing, with links to where each point came from.

body.text: The newest briefing shows at the top. Older ones are under **Earlier briefs**.
For a new competitor, press **Discover sources** first, then **Run research**.
Reviewing changes

Watched pages are checked every day. Important changes appear under **Changes to review**, each marked **critical**, **important**, **minor** or **noise**, with a summary and the before-and-after wording.

items: Read the summary and compare **Before** with **After**.
Press **Mark reviewed** once you've dealt with it, or **Dismiss as noise** if it doesn't matter.

body.text: Reviewed and dismissed changes move to **History**, so you have a record of what was seen and when.

title: Customer cases: the help desk
summary: Work customer questions, service concerns and requests from one shared queue.

body.text: **Customer cases** is your shared help desk. Each case is one customer question or concern, from first message to resolved, so nothing gets lost in someone's inbox.
The counters at the top

rows: The customer wrote last and is waiting for you
Cases with customer messages nobody has read, in the current view

body.text: Finding cases

items: **Work queues** on the left: Unassigned, Mine, Open, Pending, Closed and All, each with a count.
**Mailboxes** narrow the list to one team's queue.
**Tags** narrow it to one label.
Search by subject, description or case number (C-…), and filter by type.

body.text: Cases waiting for you are marked **Customer replied**. Unread ones show a count and a bold subject.
Opening a new case

items: Press **New case**.
Choose the customer and, if you use them, the mailbox.
Fill in the details and create it.

body.text: Depending on your permissions you see every case or only your own and your team's. Customers can also open cases themselves from the customer portal, and emails to a mailbox's address become cases automatically.

title: Working a customer case
summary: Reply to the customer, leave notes for your team, use saved replies, and set the status, owner, priority and tags.

body.text: Opening a case shows the whole conversation with the customer, and the case's details beside it. Opening it marks the customer's messages as read.
Reading the conversation

items: Customer messages are on the left, your team's replies on the right.
**Internal notes** have an amber background — the customer never sees them.
Small centred lines show events such as a change of status.

body.text: Replying or leaving a note

items: In the box at the bottom, choose **reply** (to the customer) or **note** (for your team only).
Use **Insert a saved reply…** to drop in a ready-made answer.
Optionally set the status as you send: Pending customer, Open, Resolved or Closed.
Send.

body.text: Check you're on **reply** before sending something meant for the customer, and on **note** for anything that's only for your team.
The case's details

On the right you can change the **Status**, **Assignee**, **Priority** and **Mailbox** — each saves as soon as you pick it. Type a tag name to add a tag; remove one with its ✕. You'll also see the customer's contact details, their vehicle if one is linked, attachments, and their other cases.
If someone else changed the case while you were writing, your reply isn't sent and you're asked to refresh first — so two people never overwrite each other.

title: Help desk settings: mailboxes, saved replies and tags
summary: Set up help desk mailboxes with their own email address, signature and auto-reply, ready-made replies, and tags.

body.text: **Settings → Help desk** sets up the mailboxes, saved replies and tags your team uses on customer cases. You need permission to manage cases.
Mailboxes
A mailbox is a separate queue — for example "Support" and "Workshop" — each with its own colour, signature and email address.

items: Press **New mailbox**.
Enter a name and pick a colour.
Optionally enter an **Inbox address**: email sent to that address becomes a case in this mailbox. Point that address at the inbox connected under **Settings → Email**.
Optionally add a **Signature**, added to replies from this mailbox.
Tick **Send an auto-reply when a new ticket arrives by email** and write the message if you'd like customers to get an acknowledgement.
Keep **Active** ticked and save.

body.text: The auto-reply goes once per new emailed case, never to automatic or no-reply senders, with the mailbox signature added.
Saved replies

items: Press **New reply**.
Give it a title, choose which mailbox it's for (or **All mailboxes**) and write the reply.
Save. It appears under **Insert a saved reply…** on cases.

body.text: Tags
Tags are made on the spot while working a case. This page lists them all, so you can remove any you no longer use.
